requirement: Authenticate a WebSocket from its token query parameter before accepting, closing unknown or missing tokens with code 1008, then greet the user, echo text upper-cased until bye closes with 1000, and keep an online set that is cleaned up however the socket ends.
skeleton: TOKENS table and ONLINE set with reset_db, and one websocket route that closes with 1008 before accept on a bad token, then accepts, tracks the user, loops over receive_text and removes the user in finally.
caption: Authenticated WebSockets in FastAPI. TOKENS maps tokens to user names and ONLINE records who is connected; reset_db clears it. The /ws route takes an optional token query parameter and looks it up; when no user matches, including a missing token, it closes the socket with status.WS_1008_POLICY_VIOLATION before accepting and returns. Otherwise it accepts, adds the user to ONLINE, sends a hello message naming the user, and loops on receive_text: the text bye closes the socket with WS_1000_NORMAL_CLOSURE, anything else is answered with the user and the text upper-cased. A WebSocketDisconnect from the client ends the loop quietly, and a finally block always removes the user from ONLINE. The fixture asserts that tok-ada gets a hello, an upper-cased echo of ping, and a close with code 1000 after bye with nobody left online, that a missing token and a forged token both end with WebSocketDisconnect code 1008 and nobody online, and that bob is listed in ONLINE while connected and removed after the client disconnects.

plan.intent: Only let known users hold an echo connection
constraints: Missing or unknown tokens are closed with code 1008 before accept
Messages are echoed upper-cased with the user name
The text bye closes the socket with code 1000
The user is removed from ONLINE however the connection ends
Client disconnects raise WebSocketDisconnect, which ends the loop quietly

rationale.teaches: Closing with WS_1008_POLICY_VIOLATION before accept for failed auth, and try/except WebSocketDisconnect/finally for presence tracking.
rationale.why: Wrong close codes, a lookup that falls back to the raw token, or presence left behind on disconnect all look fine on the happy path, so the fixture checks close codes and ONLINE after every ending.

ops.docstring: WebSocket echo that authenticates before accepting the connection.

ops.stmt: from fastapi import FastAPI, WebSocket, WebSocketDisconnect, status

ops.source:
@app.websocket("/ws")
async def echo(websocket: WebSocket, token: str | None = None) -> None:
    """Reject unknown tokens with 1008, then echo text upper-cased until bye."""
    user = TOKENS.get(token or "")
    if user is None:
        await websocket.close(code=status.WS_1008_POLICY_VIOLATION)
        return
    await websocket.accept()
    ONLINE.add(user)
    try:
        await websocket.send_json({"hello": user})
        while True:
            text = await websocket.receive_text()
            if text == "bye":
                await websocket.close(code=status.WS_1000_NORMAL_CLOSURE)
                return
            await websocket.send_json({"user": user, "echo": text.upper()})
    except WebSocketDisconnect:
        return
    finally:
        ONLINE.discard(user)

candidates.why_wrong: Rejected sockets close with 1003 instead of the 1008 policy violation code.
An unknown token falls back to itself as the user name, so forged tokens connect.
Users are never removed from ONLINE, so presence outlives every connection.
Only upper-case BYE ends the session, so bye is echoed instead of closing.
Text is echoed unchanged instead of upper-cased.
